title: How does a river change from source to mouth?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why does a river get wider downstream?

explain.say: Follow a river from its start to its end and it changes character. The graph shows its long profile: steep near the source, high in the hills, and flattening out towards the sea.

draw.text: How does a river change from source to mouth?

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a river from source to sea. Look at the source, the upper course and the tributary. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: How does a river change from source to mouth?

explain.say: In the upper course the slope is steep and the channel narrow and rocky. The river cuts down hard, carving V-shaped valleys, rapids and waterfalls.
In the middle course the land is gentler. Tributaries join, so the river carries more water, grows wider and deeper, and swings from side to side in bends called meanders.
In the lower course it flows across a broad, flat floodplain, carrying fine mud. At its mouth it meets the sea or a lake, often dropping that mud in an estuary or delta.

faq.a: At its source, which can be a spring, a lake, a melting glacier or boggy ground in the hills that collects rain. Small streams then join together.
asks: What is the source of a river?

faq.q: Why does a river get wider downstream?
faq.a: Tributaries keep joining, so there is more and more water to carry. On gentle land the river also erodes sideways more than downward, widening its channel and valley.
asks: Why is a river bigger near the sea?

faq.a: The mouth is where a river ends by flowing into the sea, a lake or a bigger river. Many mouths are wide estuaries where fresh and salt water mix, or deltas built of mud.

faq.q: Where does a river flow fastest?
faq.a: Mountain streams look fastest, tumbling over rocks, but much of their energy is lost to friction in a rough, shallow bed. Lower down, the bigger, smoother channel often lets water flow just as fast or faster.
asks: Is a river faster in the mountains?

faq.a: A tributary is a smaller river or stream that flows into a bigger one; the place where they meet is a confluence. The Amazon has more than 1,000 tributaries.

facts: The Nile, about 6,650 kilometres long, is usually listed as the world's longest river, though some measurements give the title to the Amazon.
The Amazon carries more water than any other river, about a fifth of all the river water reaching the oceans.

quiz.say: Which part of a river usually has waterfalls and V-shaped valleys?
quiz.show: Waterfalls and V-shaped valleys are found in the…
quiz.why: In the steep upper course the river cuts downward hard, making V-shaped valleys, rapids and waterfalls.

wrong.1: The lower course is flat and broad, with a wide floodplain.
wrong.2: At the mouth the river slows and drops mud, rather than cutting down.
